claim: Sabah State Museum's main building is shaped like a Rungus longhouse and holds an eclectic collection.
quote: Sabah Museum, Kota Kinabalu, Malaysia. Attractions. The main museum building is styled after a Rungus longhouse.

claim: The museum displays human skulls from Sabah's headhunting past and a whale skeleton hung in the main hall.
quote: human skulls from Sabah's headhunting past... a massive whale skeleton hanging in the main hall... the shape of the Longus longhouse, and the beams... resemble the Somasau dancers with outstretched arms.

claim: Monsopiad village keeps 42 real human skulls of the headhunter Monsopiad's adversaries in the House of Skulls.
quote: the legendary house of Monsopiad's descendants where the 42 skulls of his adversaries are kept... Monsopiad is the name of the most popular Kadazan headhunter, a legendary warrior who harvested 42 human skulls.

claim: Monsopiad Cultural Village in Penampang is run by the warrior's descendants, about 15 minutes from KK.
quote: Monsopiad Cultural Village... home of the headhunters... located in Penampang, 15 minutes away from Kota Kinabalu City, home to the largest ethnic group in Sabah known as the Kadazans.

claim: Mari Mari Cultural Village is a living open-air museum of five Sabah tribes with demonstrations of fire-starting, blowpipes and tattooing; skulls mark its headhunting heritage.
quote: Mari Mari Cultural Village is an open-air museum dedicated to preserving the traditions, culture, and history of northern Borneo's indigenous communities... blowpipe making, starting a fire from bamboo, and tattoo-making.

claim: Mari Mari is about 25 minutes from KK and recreates the homes of the Dusun, Rungus, Lundayeh, Murut and Bajau.
quote: Mari Mari Cultural Village | Living Heritage of Sabah, Borneo.

claim: Rumah Terbalik near Tamparuli is a fully furnished kampung house built completely upside down, 30 min from KK.
quote: The Upside Down House is located in Tamparuli, Sabah... a traditional Sabah kampung house fully equipped with kitchen, living room, bedrooms, toilet, veranda and garden viewed in an upside down perspective.

claim: Rumah Terbalik is listed in the Malaysia Book of Records as the country's first upside-down house (2012).
quote: Rumah Terbalik has been listed within the Malaysia Book of Records as being the first upside down house of Malaysia as of February 2012.

claim: The site pairs the upside-down house with a 3D Wonders Museum, the first of its kind in Borneo.
quote: Rumah Terbalik & 3D Wonders Museum... uniquely themed galleries, the first of its kind in Borneo.

claim: Abandoned colonial-era houses around KK draw urban explorers and circulate on social media as creepy ruins.
quote: Creepy abandoned house draws attention.

claim: Abandoned colonial mansions on Signal Hill above KK are documented by urbex YouTubers, with graffiti and city views.
quote: Abandoned Mansions At Signal Hill, Kota Kinabalu, Sabah.

claim: Kinarut Mansion, a rare 1910-1914 stone house south of KK, is now an abandoned ruin rumoured to be haunted.
quote: built from 1910 to 1914 and was one of the few stone houses that existed in North Borneo.

claim: Kinarut Mansion features on lists of Malaysia's haunted homes, with reports of apparitions and eerie voices.
quote: Locals have claimed the place is haunted, with reports of seeing apparitions and hearing eerie voices at night.

claim: The Atkinson Clock Tower is KK's oldest structure, a wooden tower built in 1905 in memory of a district officer who died of malaria.
quote: built to commemorate a British, Francis George Atkinson, the first District Officer of Jesselton... his mother Mary Edith Atkinson gave a two-faced clock to Jesselton town as a tribute to the memory of her son.

claim: The all-wood tower is built of merbau hardwood, stands 15.7 m and survived the WWII razing of the city.
quote: famously survived the retreat of the Allied Forces during WWII when almost every other structure in the city was razed to the ground.

claim: A Nov 2025 beautification made the tower the start of a 500 m elevated forest walkway toward Signal Hill; entry fees RM10/RM20 begin 2026.
quote: the starting point of a 500-meter elevated forest walkway... Entry fees will be introduced in 2026: RM10 for Malaysians and RM20 for foreigners.

claim: The Double Six Monument stands on the exact Sembulan spot where a 1976 plane crash killed Sabah's chief minister and ministers; a gallery displays plane debris.
quote: Four of nine Sabah state ministers including chief minister Fuad (Donald) Stephens lost their lives... A debris of the crashed plane is on display.

claim: The monument marks the 6 June 1976 Double Six Tragedy and is erected on the crash site at Sembulan.
quote: marks the site of 6 June 1976 fatal plane crash known as the Double Six Tragedy bearing the first Chief Minister of Sabah, Tun Fuad Stephens.

claim: The crash involved a Sabah Air GAF Nomad aircraft and remains shrouded in conspiracy theories among Sabahans.
quote: 1976 Sabah Air GAF Nomad Crash (Double Six Tragedy).

claim: The Tip of Borneo is the island's northernmost point where the South China and Sulu Seas meet, marked by a bronze globe.
quote: The Tip of Borneo – Tanjung Simpang Mengayau... the northernmost tip of Borneo... marks the meeting point of the South China Sea and Sulu Sea.

claim: Tanjung Simpang Mengayau means 'junction to the battle' and was a pirate watch-point; it is ~215 km from KK.
quote: also known as Tanjung Simpang Mengayau, which means the junction to the battle at the tip.

claim: Entry to the Tip of Borneo is free, with a cafe and souvenir shop beside the globe monument and flagpole.
quote: The entry is FREE. There are a cafe, souvenir shop and washrooms.

claim: Mengkabong is a Bajau stilt village in Tuaran built over an estuary, the homes connected by plank walks.
quote: Mengkabong Water Village is a stilt village of the Bajau people in Tuaran... wooden houses built on stilts that hover above water.

claim: The Bajau are Sabah's 'sea gypsies', the second-largest ethnic group, living between land and sea.
quote: The Bajau of Kota Kinabalu: A story between land and sea.

claim: Rising seas and coastal erosion threaten the Mengkabong stilt community, forcing families to rebuild homes.
quote: Mengkabong Water Village, Sabah.

claim: The Filipino Market is run by Sulu-island immigrants and is the best place for Sabah pearls and handicrafts.
quote: managed by locals & immigrants hailing from the southern islands of Philippines... best place to look for the best hand-crafted souvenirs & varieties of Sabah pearls.

claim: The waterfront Filipino Market sells freshwater and seawater pearls that vendors customise into jewellery.
quote: Freshwater and seawater pearls in various shapes, colours and sizes are available which can easily be customized to make jewellery.

claim: A tamu is a traditional open-air gathering market of farmers, fishermen and cattle breeders unique to Sabah.
quote: Tamu (Weekly Market) in Sabah.

claim: Kota Belud's Tamu Besar features buffalo auctions, buffalo racing and beauty-queen crowning; it runs late October.
quote: witness traditional sports such as buffalo racing and the crowning of beauty queens. The annual Tamu Besar of Kota Belud.

claim: Kota Belud's Bajau are famed horsemen nicknamed the 'Cowboys of the East'.
quote: Due to their skillful horse riding skills, Bajau people are known as the 'Cowboys of the East.' Their traditional homeland is the Kota Belud district.

claim: The Tamu Besar centrepiece is a parade of Bajau horsemen in silver-decorated ceremonial regalia.
quote: The Charms Of Tamu Besar Kota Belud.

claim: Butod, the sago palm weevil grub, is eaten live in Sabah; raw it tastes of sweet coconut milk, fried like fish skin; ~RM40-45/kg.
quote: The taste of raw butod is like coconut milk with a bit of sweetness... After frying... crispy and tastes like fried fish skin... sold at US$0.25 each (RM40 – 45 per Kg).

claim: Butod and other Borneo delicacies are eaten alive as a test of bravery.
quote: 14 weird and wonderful delicacies of Sabah and Sarawak.

claim: Hinava is the Kadazan-Dusun raw-fish 'ceviche' cured in lime, ginger, shallots and chilli.
quote: the Kadazan-Dusun people in Sabah have their own version of this dish called Hinava which is made with raw fish, lime, ginger, shallots, and chilli.

claim: Sabah's synchronous fireflies mass on mangrove display trees, flashing in unison like a 'summer Christmas tree'.
quote: Fireflies gather and flash on a display tree in mangrove forest, by a number of hundreds, even thousands, to create a phenomena like Summer Christmas Tree.

claim: Firefly cruises near KK run on the Klias and Garama rivers; best viewing is on moonless nights 7-10pm.
quote: Where to See Fireflies in Sabah: Top Spots and Travel Tips.

claim: The Tambunan Rafflesia Reserve protects Rafflesia, the world's largest flower, which stinks of rot and blooms unpredictably.
quote: Tambunan Rafflesia Reserve... home to Rafflesia pricei, known as one of the world's largest and rarest flowers... emits a strong scent during bloom and only blossoms for a short period.

claim: Dream Beach at Bongawan has a 'Sky Mirror' tidal flat that reflects the sky, paired with a firefly cruise.
quote: The Sky Mirror at Dream Beach in Bongawan offers... an unusual natural mirror, and an enchanting firefly cruise.

claim: Klias river cruises seek the proboscis monkey, endemic to Borneo and nicknamed 'Dutchman' for its huge pendulous nose.
quote: the bizarre-looking proboscis monkey... endemic to Borneo... nicknamed 'Monyet Belanda' or 'Dutchman'... the huge pendulous noses used to attract mates.

claim: At Kampung Luanti in Ranau, wild river mahseer give a natural 'fish massage' in a protected stretch of the Moroli river.
quote: 'Tagal' Sungai Moroli, Kampung Luanti – Fish Massage.

claim: 'Tagal' is a Kadazan-Dusun communal no-fishing system that lets rivers recover and underpins the fish-spa.
quote: The tagal way to save nature.

claim: Pulau Tiga was the filming location of the first US Survivor and is home to a mud volcano and nearby Snake Island.
quote: Pulau Tiga, also known as Survivor Island... gained fame after being the first-ever location for the international US hit reality series 'Survivor'.

claim: Pulau Tiga's bubbling mud volcano and Snake Island (banded sea kraits) are reached by boat from Kuala Penyu; the mud volcano was temporarily closed in mid-2026 from drought.
quote: Pulau Tiga Sabah | Survivor Island & Mud Volcano Guide... the banded sea krait is prevalent in Pulau Tiga, particularly on Pulau Kalampunian Damit (Snake Island).

claim: Desa Cattle Dairy Farm in Kundasang is nicknamed 'The Little New Zealand' for its misty pastures below Mount Kinabalu.
quote: Desa Cattle Dairy Farm is known as 'The Little New Zealand' of Sabah, with a breathtaking view of the majestic Mount Kinabalu overlooking verdant pastures.

claim: The farm runs three daily visiting sessions; admission RM20 for non-Malaysian adults, ~2.5-3 h from KK.
quote: Admission is RM10 for Malaysian adults with MyKad and RM20 for non-Malaysians... about 100 km east of Kota Kinabalu.

claim: Tuaran Crocodile Farm, 30 min from KK, holds over a thousand crocodiles and runs feeding shows.
quote: the Tuaran Crocodile Farm is the largest crocodile farm in Sabah... home to over a thousand crocodiles from several species and offers crocodile feeding sessions and live shows.

claim: Established in 1986, it is Sabah's largest crocodile farm, ~30 minutes northeast of KK.
quote: Established in 1986, the Tuaran Crocodile Farm is the largest crocodile farm in Sabah and one of the most comprehensive in Malaysia.

claim: Kokol Hill, ~40 min and 800 m above KK, has a whimsical 'Elf House' Hobbit-style cottage photo spot at Kokol Haven.
quote: the Elf House at Kokol Haven Resort is a whimsical photo spot resembling a Hobbit-style cottage.

claim: Kokol Hill is Sabah's main tandem-paragliding launch over KK and the coast.
quote: Paragliding in Kota Kinabalu – Kokol Hill Borneo Flights.

claim: Tamparuli's famous suspension bridge carries a tragic legend: a Dusun maiden Solungkoi cursed the bridge so it would only stand if her British lover Robinson's blood spilled.
quote: Solungkoi cursed at the bridge, saying that it will never be able to stand strong unless Robinson's blood spilled the river.

claim: Jambatan Tamparuli over the Kiulu/Tuaran river is Sabah's most famous bridge, immortalised in a popular Kadazan folk song.
quote: Jambatan Tamparuli, the most famous bridge of Sabah.

claim: At Kaamatan, a priestess (bobohizan) selects the festival date and leads the Magavau spirit-recovery ritual on a moonlit night.
quote: ending with a public holiday on a date selected by a priestess known as the bobohizan... the chief Bobohizans... begin their journey to the padi fields during the full moonlit night.

claim: Kaamatan's Unduk Ngadau beauty pageant honours Huminodun, the maiden who in myth sacrificed herself so rice could grow.
quote: The winner represents Huminodun, the legendary maiden in Kadazan-Dusun mythology who sacrificed herself so rice could grow.

claim: The month-long Kaamatan culminates 30-31 May with feasting and rice-wine toasts in Penampang.
quote: 5 Things to know about Sabah's Harvest Festival, Pesta Kaamatan.

claim: The Murut Lansaran is a giant rope-suspended communal trampoline that bounces dancers 3-4 m up to reach a prize at the top.
quote: The Lansaran... a large platform suspended by ropes from a wooden frame, functioning as a giant trampoline... bouncing up to 3–4 metres in the air.

claim: Murut tapai rice wine is drunk communally from one jar through long bamboo straws; refusing it is rude.
quote: Tapai is served in a large communal jar from which guests drink through long bamboo straws... refusing Tapai when offered is considered impolite.

claim: In early June 2026 EUR/MYR traded around 4.69, so RM10 is roughly EUR2.10.
quote: Euro (EUR) To Malaysian Ringgit (MYR) Exchange Rate History for 2026.
